findings.title: tally.schema.json's per_id.state enum omits REFUSED, a real witness status, so grade can crash
findings.description: tally.schema.json's $defs.entry.state enum lists PRESENT, PARTIAL, REGRESSED, ABSENT, NOT-A-DEFECT, UNCLEAR, PASS, FAIL, BROKEN, BLOCKED, null. At bug-hunt grading, Passes.jl:619 sets entry["state"] = uppercase(String(r.status)) from a re-run witness, and Witnesses.jl documents/implements FIVE possible statuses: :pass, :fail, :broken, :blocked and :refused (a witness that loads something outside package/Test/stdlib, or that includes another file, is refused before it runs). :refused is missing from the enum entirely. If a witness is edited between passes to trip that refusal, entry["state"] becomes the string "REFUSED" and validate(load_schema("tally"), tally) at Passes.jl:668 then fails, throwing RoundError and crashing gbg round grade for that round.

findings.title: audit.schema.json declares staleness and severity_recheck, but nothing ever writes them
findings.description: audit.schema.json declares optional top-level properties staleness (enum clean/stale/UNCHECKABLE) and severity_recheck (an open object), but a repo-wide search finds no assignment of either key anywhere audit.json is built. audit_bank (Audit.jl:39-42) only ever sets schema_version, round, base, head, kind, covered, diffstat, executable_claims, dispositions, verdict_all_clean. The staleness check the field's name promises is computed at close time (Passes.jl:933-935 via Git.changed_paths against a["head"]) but only feeds a human-readable refusal message, never written back as audit.json's staleness. The severity re-check likewise writes a wholly separate, unschema'd file severity.json (Audit.jl:65-69, read back by key "ratings" at Passes.jl:812/907) that is never merged into audit.json's severity_recheck key.
findings.resolution_hint: Either wire audit_bank/close to actually populate staleness and severity_recheck on audit.json, or drop the two properties from audit.schema.json and give severity.json its own schema instead.

findings.title: pass.schema.json's probe_open is declared but never written by any code path
findings.description: pass.schema.json documents probe_open ("ids the quote probe found still present in the corpus... The probe may open an id, never close one"). No code in src or ext writes the literal key "probe_open" anywhere. The quote-probe results are computed at Passes.jl:389 and written under the unrelated key quote_still_stands to a separate file probe.json (Passes.jl:391-392), and separately handed to the act/state verifiers as quote_probe in their args (Passes.jl:394) — never folded back into pass.toml, which (built at Passes.jl:373-377) carries no probe_open key at all.
findings.resolution_hint: Either have pass open/grade write the probe's surviving ids into probe_open on pass.toml, or remove the property from pass.schema.json since the mechanism lives entirely in probe.json today.

findings.title: carried.schema.json alone declares JSON Schema draft-07 while every sibling schema declares 2020-12
findings.description: Every other file under schema/ opens with "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema". carried.schema.json alone opens with "$schema": "http://json-schema.org/draft-07/schema#". Schema.jl's validator ignores $schema entirely (it is not in the documented keyword subset at Schema.jl:4), so this has no runtime effect, but it is the one file in the fleet's shared schema surface that misstates its own dialect, in a package whose organizing principle is one shared shape for the fleet.
findings.resolution_hint: Change carried.schema.json's $schema to "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema" to match every other file in schema/.
